# 1.2.40 - the harness was lying, and three fixes were built on what it said

**Nothing promotes `#interface` any more, and that was the whole mistake.** The
curtain is a fixed sibling at z-index 1, and since the theme shipped this layer
wrote `z-index: 1` onto Foundry's `#interface` as well, on the stated grounds
that without a stacking context of its own the whole interface would go under
the glass. That was checked against the module's own audit page, and the audit
page had Foundry's DOM wrong in two ways: the board on the wrong side of
`#interface`, and none of the interface's columns carrying the z-index Foundry
actually gives them. With the real numbers the curtain at 1 is already above the
board at 0 and already below the columns at 30, and removing the promotion
changes the rendered page by zero pixels. What the promotion did do was make a
full-screen box into a positioned full-screen box over the map - which is what
took the map's clicks in the first place - and it is the one arrangement in
which a board that ever moved inside `#interface` would paint above the glass
and make the theme vanish over the map entirely. The audit page has been
corrected to Foundry's real layout so this cannot be reasoned about wrongly
again.

**The lid repair no longer builds a lid of its own.** 1.2.39 made `#interface`
transparent to the pointer and pinned every child that was hit-testable back to
`auto`. Reading what each child asks for is right; what was missing was that a
child which COVERS THE BOARD is not a control, it is the next lid down, so
pinning it just moved the fault one level deeper. It now refuses to pin
anything that spans the map. On a stock client it pins nothing at all, and the
repair stays only for the case it was written for: somebody else giving
`#interface` a layer of its own.

**The room outline has been painting in an impossible colour.** Under this theme
the outline of the room your token stands in is meant to wear the state colour,
the one the curtain's seams wear - and it never has. `--drpg-glass-accent` is a
registered custom property, which is what lets the interface interpolate it
through a colour change, and a registered colour computes to its resolved
`rgb(...)` form. The reader handed that to a parser that reads hex, so every
hour of the day came back as not-a-number. Fixed, and the outline is thinner
under this theme as asked: a seam rather than a sprite outline, roughly half the
width, with its keyline thinned in proportion so the border reads as the same
object drawn finer. Monokuma Legacy keeps the chunky line to the pixel. The
gradient thrown out of a doorway takes the same colour, for the same reason -
it is marking the gap in a border that stops either side of it, and in any other
colour it reads as a different object.

**And the outline follows the hour now.** It was read once, when you walked in,
and then stood in that colour until you walked out. Nothing was going to correct
it: the fog's repaint only ever takes an outline down, and its signature carries
no colour term. The colour is now re-applied rather than the room re-drawn -
watched on the body's own attributes, because the attribute changing IS the
colour changing, with nothing in between to get the order wrong.

**Windows are the size of their content, and their content fills them.** The cap
1.2.39 added was `74ch` on the box the frame measures itself from, and under this
face 74ch is 385px while the frame is floored at 544 - a 174px dead band down
the right of every prose window. Two things were wrong with it: `ch` resolves
against each element's own font and these dialogs have three, so one cap was
three different edges; and capping that box stops it stretching to the frame,
which is what leaves the band. The measure now sits one level in, as a single
length, so the frame shrink-wraps to it instead of standing wider than it - and
because it is a length rather than a list of text tags, it also holds for content
that is not a paragraph, which used to escape the cap and run edge to edge.

**The Settings window fits.** Its overflow was not a width rule at all. Foundry
sets `white-space: nowrap` on inline code, and the glass diagnostic at the bottom
of that window is one unbroken 1500px line, so the whole window was stretched to
it and everything above - the interface-scale slider included - was dragged off
the right edge and clipped. The line wraps now, and nothing else had to change.

**The clock and Despair explainers get their text back.** Same fault one level
down: their card is capped at 46 characters, which under VT323 is 239px of text
in a 544px window. 1.2.39 tried to fix that by shrinking the frame to the card,
which was the wrong way round twice - it made a window already reported as too
narrow narrower still, and the rule was one class short of the one above it, so
it never won and never did anything. The card grows instead, and roughly doubles.

**The GM Panel button sits on the tiles' edge.** It was centred in the left
column, which put it half the column's leftover space to the right of the scene
controls - 105px on a wide column, 19px on a narrow one, so no single nudge could
have been right for both. It shares the tiles' start edge now, by construction,
at any interface scale.

Also: the rail's fallback box is sized from what the rail actually measures and
scales with the interface, instead of being smaller than the rail has ever been;
the strip beside the Despair rail no longer takes its height from the rail's
tilted bounding box; the curtain's self-check now asks whether a block stands in
its OWN pane rather than any pane in its column, which is the check that would
have caught a block losing its glass to a neighbour; and `drpgGlassDebug()`
reports the hit stack over the map, what the module pinned, and every pane
against the block it was cut for.
